revealWordProblem.title: Apply: A Game of Golf
revealWordProblem.text: Golf scores are measured as strokes over or under par. Par is the number of golf strokes considered necessary to get the ball in the hole, so a score under par is written as a negative integer and a score over par is written as a positive integer. The scorecard shows six players' scores relative to par after seven holes of a 9-hole round (par = 35): Evelyn -2, Brielle +1, Terrance 0, Reginald -3, Sofia +4, Francisco +2. Order the six scores from least to greatest to rank the players from first place (the current leader) to last place. Who is winning after 7 holes, and who has the most strokes to make up?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A golf score card with par equal to 35, showing six players' scores and how far each is over or under par.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: From least to greatest, the scores are -3, -2, 0, +1, +2, +4, which ranks the players Reginald, Evelyn, Terrance, Brielle, Francisco, Sofia. Reginald is winning after 7 holes because -3 is the least score — it is farthest left on the number line, meaning he used the fewest strokes compared to par. Sofia is in last place because +4 is the greatest score, farthest right on the number line, meaning she has used the most strokes over par.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Compare and Order Integers is thinking that a negative number with a bigger digit is the bigger value — for example, believing -15 is greater than -8 because 15 is greater than 8. It's the opposite for negatives: the number farther to the left on the number line (farther from zero) is always the LESSER value, so -15 < -8. Before you submit, check your comparison against the number line, not just the digits.

level3.prompt: A student says: 'Negative numbers are always less than positive numbers, so -100 is less than 1.' Is this correct? Now the student says: '-100 is less than -1 because 100 is greater than 1.' Is THIS correct? Explain the difference.
level3.sentenceFrame: The first statement is ___ because ___. The second statement is ___ because with negative numbers, ___. On the number line, -100 is ___ of -1, so ___.
level3.hint: Use examples with specific coordinates to explain your thinking.
hints: Two separate claims to judge — an answer can be right while the REASON is wrong. Check each on a number line.
For -100 vs -1, don't compare 100 and 1. Compare positions: which number sits farther below zero?
Place -100 and 1 first: negative vs positive settles claim 1. Then place -100 and -1 and see which is farther left.
level3.explanation: The first statement is true: -100 is negative and 1 is positive, so -100 sits left of 1 on the number line and is less. The second answer, -100 < -1, is also true, but the reason given is wrong — it is not because 100 > 1, it is because -100 lies 100 units below zero while -1 lies only 1 unit below, putting -100 farther left.
level3.explanationEs: El primer enunciado es verdadero: -100 es negativo y 1 es positivo, así que -100 queda a la izquierda de 1 en la recta numérica y es menor. La segunda respuesta, -100 < -1, también es verdadera, pero la razón que da es incorrecta: no es porque 100 > 1, sino porque -100 está 100 unidades por debajo de cero mientras que -1 está solo 1 unidad por debajo, lo que deja a -100 más a la izquierda.
level3.promptEs: Un estudiante dice: 'Los números negativos siempre son menores que los positivos, así que -100 es menor que 1.' ¿Es correcto? Ahora el estudiante dice: '-100 es menor que -1 porque 100 es mayor que 1.' ¿Es correcto ESTO? Explica la diferencia.
hintsEs: Hay dos afirmaciones que juzgar: una respuesta puede ser correcta aunque la RAZÓN esté mal. Revisa cada una en una recta numérica.
Para −100 frente a −1, no compares 100 y 1. Compara posiciones: ¿qué número queda más abajo de cero?
Coloca primero −100 y 1: negativo contra positivo resuelve la afirmación 1. Luego coloca −100 y −1 y ve cuál está más a la izquierda.
